body.text: What happens on Day 1, Day 2, Day 3 and Day 4 of a hair transplant visit?

On a standard four-day visit, Day 1 covers airport arrival, hotel check-in, and pre-op blood work or consultation; Day 2 is the full six-to-eight-hour procedure under local anesthesia; Day 3 is dedicated to hotel rest and bandage removal; and Day 4 includes the first clinic wash and departure clearance.

Knowing how many days istanbul hair transplant visits require starts with respecting the pace of outpatient surgery. As [UK NHS hair transplant guidance](https://www.nhs.uk/tests-and-treatments/cosmetic-procedures/cosmetic-surgery/hair-transplant/) notes, a hair transplant is performed under local anesthesia and usually takes a full day without requiring an overnight hospital stay, though large cases can span two surgical days. Planning a realistic buffer prevents rushing from the operating chair straight into airport security.

body.text: Is a 3-day trip enough or is 4–5 days more comfortable?

A compressed 3-day trip—landing Monday, undergoing surgery Tuesday, and flying home Wednesday—leaves zero margin for flight delays, two-day sessions, or post-op swelling. Spending 4 to 5 days in Istanbul is markedly more comfortable, especially if you are flying long-haul or want an unhurried in-person consultation before surgery.

Medical travel authorities including the [CDC Yellow Book](https://www.cdc.gov/yellow-book/hcp/health-care-abroad/medical-tourism.html) highlight that combining surgery with long flights increases fatigue and blood-clot risk, and recommend securing English-language medical records and clear follow-up plans before departing. Adding one extra night in a quiet, well-located hotel costs a fraction of your trip budget while letting your physician inspect early healing on Day 3 or Day 4. For flight timing and cabin precautions, read our guide on [flying home after a hair transplant](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/flying-after-hair-transplant).
Can you tour Sultanahmet or take a Bosphorus cruise before surgery?

Yes—sightseeing in Sultanahmet, Karaköy, or along the Bosphorus works smoothly before your procedure, provided you arrive one or two days early and keep pre-op evenings rested and alcohol-free. After surgery, you should skip crowded landmarks, steep hills, ferries in wind or sun, and hammams to protect fragile grafts.

Sequencing leisure strictly ahead of surgery is one of the simplest ways to enjoy Istanbul without risking clinical recovery. At [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/about), our founders design calm pre-surgery days around your clinic schedule through our [medical tourism coordination service](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/services/medical-tourism). Use this practical pacing checklist when booking flights:

items: Add 1–2 pre-op days if you want to visit Hagia Sophia, Topkapı Palace, or take a private Bosphorus boat ride.
Choose a hotel with quiet rooms, reliable air conditioning, elevator access, and minimal traffic distance to your clinic.
Keep surgery evening and the following 48 hours completely free of restaurant bookings, tours, or shopping.
Pack loose button-up or zip-front shirts so nothing pulls over your head on departure day.

body.text: When does the first clinic wash take place?

Most Istanbul clinics perform the first supervised scalp wash 48 hours after surgery—typically on Day 4 of a standard itinerary—though some physicians start gentle foam cleansing as early as 24 to 36 hours or wait until Day 3 post-op. Your operating doctor sets the exact washing protocol.

Clinical research published on [PubMed Central (PMC)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4517519/) emphasizes that gentle daily washing starting around two days post-operation helps prevent heavy crusting, while warning that forcefully removing adherent scabs during days two through five can dislodge newly implanted grafts. During the clinic wash, staff apply softening lotion, rinse with lukewarm low-pressure water, and demonstrate how you will wash safely at home over the next 10 days. Before checking out, confirm your clinic provides written English aftercare instructions and a clear post-op contact channel, as advised by [UK NHS cosmetic surgery abroad guidance](https://www.nhs.uk/tests-and-treatments/cosmetic-procedures/advice/cosmetic-surgery-abroad/). You can also check [how ITO coordinates medical travel](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/how-ito-coordinates-medical-travel) to see how we structure wash-day logistics.

faq.q: What is the minimum number of nights needed in Istanbul for a hair transplant?
faq.a: Three nights (four days) is the practical minimum for most single-day procedures, allowing arrival, surgery, a recovery day, and the first supervised wash before flying home.

faq.q: When is a 5-day or 6-day Istanbul stay necessary?
faq.a: Allow 5 to 6 days if your physician plans a two-day surgical session, if you want 1–2 days of sightseeing before surgery, or if you are flying long-haul to North America, Australia, or the Gulf.

faq.q: Can I go out for dinner the evening after my hair transplant?
faq.a: Most doctors advise resting in your hotel room on surgery evening, ordering room service, keeping your head propped up, and avoiding bending, alcohol, or bumped doorways.

faq.q: Does Istanbul traffic affect clinic and airport transfer timing?
faq.a: Yes. Cross-Bosphorus or Istanbul Airport (IST) transfers can take 45 to 90 minutes depending on rush hour. Choosing a hotel close to your clinic reduces post-op transit stress.

faq.q: What if my clinic schedules my consultation and surgery on the same morning?
faq.a: Same-day consultation and surgery are common in Istanbul, but joint [BAHRS and Turkish guidelines](https://www.bahrs.co.uk/news/uk-and-turkish-medical-associations-unite-to-issue-minimum-guidelines-for-hair-transplant-surgery/) recommend reviewing your doctor's written plan in advance so you never feel rushed into consent.
